title: Use a mask to select pixels
summary: A mask is an image that marks which pixels to include. In this operation, a nonzero mask value allows the source pixel through.
introduction: A mask is an image that marks which pixels to include. In this operation, a nonzero mask value allows the source pixel through. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain use a mask to select pixels
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A mask is an image that marks which pixels to include. In this operation, a nonzero mask value allows the source pixel through.

blocks.code:
import cv2
import numpy as np

image = np.array([[10, 20], [30, 40]], dtype=np.uint8)
mask = np.array([[255, 0], [0, 255]], dtype=np.uint8)
selected = cv2.bitwise_and(image, image, mask=mask)
print(selected.tolist())
blocks.title: Use a mask to select pixels

blocks.text: The output is [[10, 0], [0, 40]]. The mask keeps the two diagonal pixels and blocks the other two.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: The mask needs matching image width and height and a suitable single-channel type.
